subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group isolation stay within configurable sender/topic session routing and explicit thread-bound subagents, or should OpenClaw add automatic per-sender group subagent lifecycle with per-user skills, config, memory, admin controls, quotas, and cleanup?
rationale: The requested behavior is not a narrow bug fix; it changes Feishu product behavior, persistent session identity, per-agent configuration, skill authorization, memory isolation, and group-message security boundaries.

options.title: Approve A Feishu Design First
options.body: Define a plugin-owned design for sender identity, memory namespace, skill/config writes, quotas, lifecycle cleanup, and live proof before implementation.

options.title: Constrain To Existing Seams
options.body: Keep groupSessionScope, bindings, and explicit thread-bound subagents as the supported pattern, then document the recommended Feishu group setup.

options.title: Split The Request
options.body: Break the broad proposal into separate canonical issues for sender session isolation, threading ergonomics, user skill preferences, and lifecycle/admin controls.

recommendation.title: Approve A Feishu Design First
recommendation.body: Define a plugin-owned design for sender identity, memory namespace, skill/config writes, quotas, lifecycle cleanup, and live proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is primarily Feishu plugin product behavior, and the package metadata names @m1heng as the community maintainer.
